Basics: Uses 99 public registers, these are referenced by a 2-character integers e.g 01, 99, 28
Registers can be surrounded by ( and ) to specify them as Duplicates of the previous mentioned Register, A register can only have ONE duplicate

Cell Commands.Description: These commands run once for each Register

All examples.]: Write the Register into the terminal
All examples.>: Print a byte from an associated Buffer; if any, using the associated register as an indexer
All examples.[: Write the Register into the associated buffer; if any
All examples.<: Read a byte from the terminal to the associated Buffer; if any, using the associated register as an indexer
All examples._: Jump base, this is a pointer that can be jumped to at any time by only ONE pointer
All examples.^: Jump, this jumps to the closest Jump base, whilst the Register dupe is NOT 0
All examples.{: Specify that a branch should be the output of an instruction branch, this MUST be at the end of a Branch
All examples.}: Specify that a branch should NOT be the output of an instruction branch, this MUST be at the end of a Branch

Splitter Commands.Decription: These commands split a command branch such that the instructions on both sides of the character run on duplicates of the input register

All examples.*: Run both sides and multiply them with each other
All examples.=: Run both sides and compare them to each other
All examples./: Run both sides and divide them by each other
All examples.%: Run both sides and modulo divides them by each other
